title: Schizophrenia, schizoaffective and bipolar disorder
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's psychiatric condition.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for mood stability.

HPI: Pt is an 85-year-old female presenting for routine psychiatric follow-up. Pt has a history of bipolar disorder. She reports feeling stable and well. She notes that while her most recent episode depressed occurred over a year ago, she has remained stable since. Pt reports no significant mood swings or sleep disturbances for over a year on lithium. She denies any current distress or functional impairment.

Medication List:
- Lithium Carbonate 300mg BID
- Lisinopril 10mg daily
- Amlodipine 5mg daily

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: No fatigue, no weight changes.
Psychiatric: Denies mood swings, denied sleep issues.
Neurological: No tremors or dizziness.
All other systems reviewed and negative.

Social History: Pt lives with her daughter. Retired. No tobacco use.

Family History: Mother had hypertension. Father had heart disease.

Vitals:
BP: 128/82
HR: 72 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 98% on RA
Weight: 145 lbs

Recent Labs:
Lithium level: 0.8 mEq/L
TSH: 2.1 mIU/L
BMP: Na 138, K 4.2, Cr 0.9, eGFR 78

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3. Appears well-groomed.
Psych: Affect is congruent and stable. Speech is clear and normal rate. Thought process is linear and goal-directed. Mood is euthymic. No signs of distress.
Physical: CTAB. RRR. Lungs clear.

Assessment:
1. Bipolar disorder, currently in full remission.
2. Stable on current lithium regimen.

Plan:
- Continue lithium carbonate 300mg BID.
- Continue current antihypertensives.
- Continue monitoring mood stability.
- Pt to return in 3 months for routine follow-up.

Electronically signed,
D. Kowalski, DO
10/14/2026
explanations: Bipolar disorder in full remission, most recent episode depressed: F31.76 (no HCC in V28).

distractors.why: The provider documents full remission, not an active episode.
